## Kyoto Family Vacation Overview
A relaxed 5-day Kyoto plan for 4 people, designed for a 7-year-old and a 72-year-old with **moderate walking only**, **2 major activities max per day**, and **rest time built in**.
Budget target stays **under 180,000 JPY total excluding flights** by mixing free sights, short transfers, and simple meals.

## 5-Day Kyoto Family Itinerary
| Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening | Rest time | Est. cost for 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| May 2 | Arrive, check in, easy lunch near Kyoto Station | Kyoto Station area stroll; short visit to Kyoto Tower base or station observatory area | Early dinner in station mall; quiet evening walk nearby | 2:00–4:00 PM hotel rest | 18,000–24,000 JPY |
| May 3 | Kiyomizu-dera with taxi drop-off and slow temple visit | Gion and Yasaka Shrine area, seated tea break | Dinner in Gion/Pontocho, then return early | 1:30–3:00 PM cafe/hotel break | 28,000–34,000 JPY |
| May 4 | Arashiyama Bamboo Grove early, then river area | Tenryu-ji gardens or monkey park only if energy is good; otherwise scenic boat/river walk | Dinner in Arashiyama or back in central Kyoto | 1:00–3:30 PM rest at hotel | 30,000–38,000 JPY |
| May 5 | Fushimi Inari lower shrine area only, no full hike | Nishiki Market tasting lunch and nearby shopping | Kamogawa riverside stroll and casual dinner | 2:00–4:00 PM hotel rest | 24,000–32,000 JPY |
| May 6 | Kyoto Imperial Palace Park or Maruyama Park easy morning | Souvenir stop and checkout; depart | Light final meal before leaving | Midday rest before travel | 16,000–24,000 JPY |

## Day-by-Day Family Plan
### Day 1: Easy Arrival and Low-Key Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Morning: Arrive in Kyoto, check in, and keep the first meal simple near Kyoto Station.
- Afternoon: Short, flat-area walk around Kyoto Station; if everyone feels good, visit the station’s observation spaces or nearby indoor areas.
- Evening: Early dinner, then a calm walk close to the hotel.
- Rest: Plan a full hotel break from mid-afternoon to avoid first-day fatigue.

### Day 2: Kiyomizu and Gion at a Slow Pace
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Take a taxi or bus close to Kiyomizu-dera and focus on the main temple area only.
- Afternoon: Rest at a cafe or hotel, then visit Gion and Yasaka Shrine with plenty of seated breaks.
- Evening: Have an early dinner in Gion or Pontocho and return before it gets too late.
- Rest: Keep walking segments short and avoid uphill detours.

### Day 3: Arashiyama Nature Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Start early at Arashiyama Bamboo Grove before crowds build.
- Afternoon: Choose one main add-on: Tenryu-ji gardens for a calmer visit, or skip extra sightseeing and enjoy the river area instead.
- Evening: Eat in Arashiyama if energy is good, otherwise head back for a quieter dinner near the hotel.
- Rest: Schedule a long hotel break after lunch.

### Day 4: Fushimi Inari and Food Stops
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Visit only the lower Fushimi Inari shrine area; do not attempt the full mountain climb.
- Afternoon: Rest, then go to Nishiki Market for light tasting and souvenir browsing.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Rest, then go to Nishiki Market for light tasting and souvenir browsing, Kyoto, Japan
- Evening: Enjoy a relaxed riverside walk along the Kamogawa and a casual dinner.
- Rest: Keep the shrine visit short to protect the grandparent’s energy.

### Day 5: Gentle Finish and Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg
- Morning: Visit Kyoto Imperial Palace Park or another flat, easy walking area.
Media: Alt=Morning: Visit Kyoto Imperial Palace Park or another flat, easy walking area, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Use the rest of the day for packing, checkout, and a final souvenir stop.
- Evening: Have a simple farewell meal before departure.
- Rest: Leave generous buffer time for luggage and transit.

## Budget Fit for 4 People
- Lodging: **70,000–95,000 JPY** for 4 nights in a family room or 2 rooms
- Food: **45,000–60,000 JPY** for mostly casual meals
- Local transport: **12,000–18,000 JPY** using buses, taxis for steep areas, and short rail rides
- Admissions and small extras: **15,000–25,000 JPY**
- Total target: **142,000–198,000 JPY**

Best way to stay under **180,000 JPY**:
- Choose a hotel near Kyoto Station or central Kyoto
- Use taxis only for steep or tiring segments
- Keep paid attractions to 1 per day, with one free/low-cost stop
- Eat breakfast at the hotel or convenience stores on some days
